html:
The Reserve Bank of India is India's central bank. It opened on 1 April 1935, issues the rupee, sets interest rates and oversees the country's banks.

Before it, government accounts and some central banking jobs were done by the Imperial Bank, which grew out of the Bank of Bengal. A royal commission on Indian currency in 1926 called for a true central bank, and a law of 1934 set it up. It began as a bank owned by private shareholders, based in Calcutta, and moved to Bombay in 1937.

India nationalised it in 1949. Its jobs grew with the planned economy: it directed credit to farming and industry and managed tight controls on foreign exchange. In the 1991 crisis it shipped gold abroad to raise loans, just before economic liberalisation began.

Since 2016 it has targeted a set rate of inflation. It backed the Unified Payments Interface, which made India a world leader in instant digital payments, and in 2016 it carried out the government's sudden withdrawal of most banknotes. It is modelled in part on the Bank of England.
sum: The Reserve Bank of India is India's central bank. It opened on 1 April 1935, issues the rupee, sets interest rates and oversees the country's banks.
